speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've presented with right leg weakness, unsteady gait, multiple falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To better understand the underlying cause, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been occurring and if there was any recent head trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details; the combination of progressive cognitive decline with recent focal neurological signs like right leg weakness is concerning. Have you noticed any changes in his vision, such as double vision or blurred vision, or any slurred speech? 

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain - Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years. Social history: Information not provided

speaker: Patient
text: The patient is somnolent and slightly confused, oriented to person but not to place or time. Mild lymphadenopathy is noted. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neurocysticercosis with cysticercosis of the brain and meningeal involvement.

The mention of "Gastroenteritis" and "lymphadenopathy" strongly suggests an infectious etiology, likely a parasitic infection like neurocysticercosis given the subacute onset of cognitive decline, focal weakness, and behavioral changes. I have requested the MRI images to confirm the presence of cysts or calcifications in the brain.
